incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Québec), CQLR c S-31.1, ss 3-31; optional federal incorporation under Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss 8-17
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Services en ligne CLIC (Centre de Liaison Informatique Client)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation (statuts constitutifs), model form under Regulation respecting the Business Corporations Act (Québec)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement under the QBCA; shares may be issued without initial cash payment, but consideration must be credited to stated capital
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporators approve the articles of incorporation filed under the Business Corporations Act (Québec) and that the corporation be constituted upon issuance of the certificate of incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the corporation accept the subscribers' application for the initial allotment of common shares, with consideration credited to stated capital. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be established at the address in the articles, within Québec, and that the Registraire des entreprises du Québec be advised. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the named individuals be elected directors and the following officers be appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Corporate Secretary. RESOLVED FINALLY, that banking authorities be established and the opening of accounts for marine bunkering operations be authorized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online CLIC portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS-preferred name search on the REQ online portal; verify French-language compliance under the Charter of the French Language; submit a name reservation request and pay the prescribed fee; the reservation is valid for 90 days; keep the reservation number for use in the articles of incorporation.
required_dossiers: NUANS or REQ name search report
Consent letter if name contains an individual's name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised name request within the reservation period or within 30 days of refusal; alternatively, apply to the Superior Court of Québec for judicial review of the registrar's decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - CLIC electronic filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the model-form articles of incorporation specifying the corporate name, share classes and rights, restrictions on share transfers, number and names of first directors, and registered office address; file electronically via CLIC and pay the incorporation and registration fees; the filing must be in French or bilingual.
required_dossiers: Consent of first directors to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a notice of refusal for incompleteness, cure by filing corrective amended articles (articles modificatifs or rectificatifs) within 30 days; request expedited reconsideration via the CLIC 'révision' function.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Enterprise Registration (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance, REQ issues the certificate of incorporation (certificat de constitution) and assigns the enterprise number (NEQ); a notice of the articles is published in the Gazette officielle du Québec; verify that the registered office address appears correctly in the enterprise register.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation issued by REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request rectification of any error in the certificate or register through a CLIC correction filing within 60 days; late corrections may require articles of rectification approved by the board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Resolutions, Bylaws, and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation itself acting through directors at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first organizational meeting of directors; adopt bylaws (règlements administratifs); approve share subscriptions and issue share certificates; elect officers; open the statutory minute book containing the share register, directors register, and register of individuals with significant control; seal and banking resolutions to be recorded.
required_dossiers: Share subscription lists and share certificates
Registers (shareholders, directors, individuals with significant control)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a validity defect is detected in the corporate records, the board may ratify or amend the resolutions retroactively; ensure all registers are brought current to avoid penalties under QBCA s 40-51.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Social Registrations (GST-HST, QST, Payroll, and Business Number)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register online for the federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account via the CRA Business Registration Online system; register with Revenu Québec for the Québec Sales Tax (TVQ/QST), employer source deductions, and the contribution to the Fonds des services de santé (if applicable); obtain the NEQ and confirm provincial tax accounts are activated before commencing bunkering operations.
required_dossiers: Federal registration form (CRA RC1 or online)
Revenu Québec registration form LM-1-V or equivalent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed or rejected, file a formal objection with Revenu Québec within 90 days; for CRA accounts, request administrative correction or call the Business Window for an expedited review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Filings and Annual Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the initial annual declaration (déclaration annuelle de mise à jour) within 60 days of the anniversary of incorporation; register any subsequent changes to directors, officers, registered office, or activities within 15 days; maintain the register of individuals with significant control and update within 15 days of any change.
required_dossiers: Updated registers of directors and significant control
Proof of corporate activity commencement (bunkering services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late-filing penalties may be waived on a showing of due diligence; file a regularization declaration through CLIC and pay the penalty amount; repeated non-compliance may lead to dissolution by the registrar, curable by reactivation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Régie de l'énergie du Québec (fuel distribution licensing) and Transport Canada - Marine Safety and Security (marine bunkering operations)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence de distributeur de produits pétroliers (Petroleum Products Distributor Licence) and Marine Fueling Operations Permit for marine terminals

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs du Québec (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II - Environmental Authorization (certificat d'autorisation) under Section 22 of the Environment Quality Act; full EIA required only for greenfield marine terminals with fuel throughput above regulatory thresholds; otherwise simplified registration with a preliminary site characterization.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with the Règlement sur les effluents des systèmes d'assainissement des eaux usées and federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations; oil and grease content below 15 mg/L. VOCs: vapour recovery and carbon canister requirements under the Règlement sur l'assainissement de l'atmosphère for marine loading operations; benzene workplace exposure limit of 0.5 ppm TWA per CNESST. Waste handling: hydrocarbon-contaminated water and slops must be declared and transported with a manifest under the Règlement sur les matières dangereuses.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire prevention service; Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) conformity inspection of petroleum equipment under the Règlement sur les installations pétrolières; CNESST occupational health and safety prevention program approval; civil security emergency response plan filed with the Ministère de la Sécurité publique du Québec and Transport Canada pollution emergency plan under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec; CRA Business Registration Online (https://www.canada.ca/), Revenu Québec Business Registration (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) from CRA for GST/HST purposes, along with a separate Quebec Establishment Number (NEQ) and QST registration from Revenu Québec. For marine fuel bunkering, the entity should complete CRA account creation through the Business Registration Online portal and Revenu Québec's Registraire des entreprises for QST and payroll deduction accounts, providing statutory proof of foreign incorporation, Quebec place of business, and expected Canadian revenue.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election in Canada; GST/HST and QST joint election for closely related corporations may apply under Excise Tax Act section 273 and Quebec Taxation Act equivalent for inter-corporate supply purposes; non-resident corporations may elect to file a separate GST/HST return for a Quebec permanent establishment through CRA Form GST494.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (GST/HST at federal level) plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST); supply of marine fuel and lubricants for international commercial shipping is generally zero-rated
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies for both GST/HST registration under Excise Tax Act and QST registration under Quebec Taxation Act; registration becomes mandatory once a foreign entity carries on commercial activity in Canada or Quebec and exceeds the CAD 30,000 threshold in a single calendar quarter or over twelve consecutive months; voluntary registration is available below threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not currently impose a nationwide real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime. CRA requires GST/HST returns and informational filings to be transmitted electronically in many cases; Revenu Québec mandates electronic billing for suppliers to Quebec public bodies through PEPPOL-based e-invoicing infrastructure and requires transmission of data required for QST returns through its online portal. Marine bunkering operators must preserve electronic invoices indefinitely and issue compliant GST/HST and QST tax invoices in French or English, including registration numbers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under the Excise Tax Act to supplies of marine fuel, lubricants, and bunkering services made to a non-resident or to a person operating a ship used exclusively in international commercial transportation or international marine commerce, provided the fuel is delivered for consumption in or removal from Canada in connection with such international voyages. The supply must be invoiced as a zero-rated export in the GST/HST and QST returns, and the supplier must hold documentation demonstrating that the buyer is a non-resident or an international carrier and that the goods were physically sold for use outside Canada or in international shipping.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency B13A Export Declaration or approved electronic equivalent)
Bill of Lading or duly signed ship manifest showing foreign port of destination
Bunker Delivery Receipt (BDR) generated by bunkering supplier and countersigned by vessel master or chief engineer
Inland or marine terminal delivery confirmation showing actual transfer of fuel or lubricants into the vessel
Final tax invoice and proof of price, volume, fuel grade, ISO 8217 specifications, and vessel IMO number
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT wire / Standby LC settlement proof
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess zero-rated export claims within the statutory limitation periods if documentation is incomplete or fails to establish the international character of the bunkering supply. Missed documentation requirements expose the entity to full GST/HST and QST clawback at the combined rate, plus arrears interest. Penalties under Excise Tax Act include a 5% penalty plus 1% per month for unreported or misstated zero-rated amounts, up to a maximum of 10% of the understated tax; on gross negligence or wilful evasion, penalties may reach 200% of the tax evaded and fines up to CAD 50,000 for summary conviction, or CAD 500,000 on indictment, with imprisonment for wider criminal tax evasion offences. Revenu Québec imposes parallel QST penalties under the Quebec Taxation Act from 5% to 25% plus interest, increased for recidivism.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BoC) is the central monetary authority; prudential supervision of banks and foreign exchange dealers is exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) under the Bank Act (Canada). Canada maintains no dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration agency, as the Canadian dollar is fully convertible and the capital account is liberalized.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies to both current account and capital account transactions under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act; no Government of Canada exchange permit or prior approval is required for profit remittance, dividend repatriation, or loan repayments. Outbound dividends from a Quebec business corporation are subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (Canada) (25% statutory, generally reduced by treaty), and distributions must satisfy the solvency test under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c S-31.1). The Investment Canada Act may require a notification or review filing for direct foreign investment above applicable WTO-asset thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canadian law imposes no statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio on export receipts. Bunker fuel sales proceeds may be held indefinitely in USD or other foreign-currency accounts at Canadian banks or abroad. All electronic fund transfers of CAD 10,000 or more are reportable by the financial institution to FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; exporters holding foreign property above CAD 100,000 must file Form T1135 annually.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD concentration for trade settlements)
Operational Account (trade finance and LC desk)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-Low. Electronic-money institutions and payment-fintech platforms (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, PayPal) operate in Canada as Money Service Businesses registered with FINTRAC and are subject to the Retail Payment Activities Act licensing framework effective 2024. Such platforms are legally usable for small-value operational disbursements (crew payroll, routine supplier payments under CAD 50,000) but are structurally unsuitable as the primary treasury rail for ISIC 5222 bunkering because they do not provide documentary letters of credit, standby LCs, bank guarantees, or ISDA-based FX forward lines, and most apply internal sectoral restrictions on marine fuel suppliers. A full-service Schedule I bank relationship remains mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance at a KYC interview in Montreal, Toronto, or another Canadian commercial centre is effectively mandatory for non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners of a marine bunkering entity, due to the Medium-Risk (Enhanced) AML classification of the sector. Remote onboarding is occasionally permitted where: (i) a Canadian-resident officer holds a valid power of attorney from the entity; (ii) the UBO completes a live video verification with the bank compliance officer; and (iii) all corporate documents are apostilled/legalized and accompanied by bank references. National Bank of Canada and Desjardins Group are the most accommodating to remote-digital structures among Quebec-based institutions, but a physical signature on the banking mandate is normally required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Vessel sanctions exposure: counterparties or supply chains touching OSFI, UN, EU, or OFAC sanctions lists, including Russia-linked Arctic LNG projects, Iranian crude carriers, or Venezuelan flagged vessels.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screening output at counterparty and voyage level; vessel background file containing IMO number, flag registry certificate, ISM and ISPS certification, 12-month AIS transponder track, charter-party and bunker order confirmation; signed attestation restricting dealings to non-sanctioned ports; transaction-level screening audit trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership structure, including layered holding companies in Panama or Marshall Islands, or discretionary trusts with undisclosed settlors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate chain chart through to natural persons; notarized certificates of incumbency; registry extracts from Revenu Quebec (Registraire des entreprises); proof of identity and tax residence for all UBOs; source-of-wealth declaration; bank reference from the prior house bank; audited organizational documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual payment patterns: cash-prepayment to shell suppliers, third-party intercompany transfers, or high-frequency USD/CAD conversions inconsistent with the invoicing cycle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Two years of audited financial statements; 12-month cash-flow forecast tied to charter/supply contracts; complete commercial pack (bunker supply agreements, purchase orders, invoices, delivery receipts, bill-of-lading evidence); AML/ATF policy manual with FINTRAC compliance procedures; written transaction profile projection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between corporate object and bank usage, e.g., registry description as general trading while actual activity is marine fuel wholesaling and physical supply.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Canadian and Quebec licence for marine fuel distribution; QST/GST registration certificates from Revenu Quebec; active buyer-supplier agreements with major trading houses; charter or terminal contracts demonstrating physical supply capability; working-capital rationale consistent with requested credit lines.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder injections via SWIFT MT103 (financing leg) or MT202/MT202COV (bank-to-bank cover), with the payment memo explicitly stating 'Paid-up share capital contribution / equity injection for ISIC 5222 marine bunkering'. All EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more are reported to FINTRAC; the receiving bank will normally pre-clear the funds into a Capital Escrow Account before releasing to the operational account. Supporting documentation must include the board resolution authorizing the share issuance, subscription agreement, certificate of good standing from the Quebec corporate registry, and, where the investment exceeds Canada's WTO thresholds, a notification filed with Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) under the Investment Canada Act.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clean supplier payments to bunker trading houses in Singapore, Rotterdam, and Houston are executed by SWIFT MT103 across CHIPS or Fedwire USD clearing, with CLS settlement for USD/CAD FX legs. High-value or performance-linked procurement uses Commercial Letters of Credit issued under UCP600 and Standby LCs under ISP98. Domestic CAD disbursements clear through Lynx (formerly LVTS) for high-value same-day payments and the Real-Time Rail (RTR) for instant low-value transfers; all outward electronic transfers above CAD 10,000 are reported to FINTRAC, and payments to sanctioned entities are blocked by automated screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX forwards (plain vanilla) under an ISDA Master Agreement
CAD/USD FX swaps (simultaneous spot and forward legs)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for CAD/USD debt servicing
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF), permitted for CAD and lesser-traded pairs, though CAD/USD is fully deliverable onshore
OTC currency options (call/put on USD/CAD), collars, and zero-cost structures
Exchange-traded CAD/USD futures on CME as a supplemental hedge
All instruments require an executed ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or Canadian Master Derivative Agreement and hedge accounting documentation under IFRS 9 for the bunker procurement cycle

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No fixed monetary threshold; mandatory contemporaneous documentation required for related-party transactions exceeding $1 million CAD
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP), Resale Price Method, Cost Plus Method, Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM), Profit Split Method
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Not applicable under Canadian law; compliance governed by General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR), substance-over-form doctrine, and beneficial ownership requirements

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income or false claims for deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction; fines up to five times evaded tax; imprisonment up to five years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for corporate tax debts; possible director disqualification, travel bans, and criminal charges

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining Canadian corporation without real business operations, decision-making, or employees in Canada
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty up to $100,000; loss of all tax benefits; application of GAAR to deny deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for unpaid taxes; potential criminal liability under Criminal Code for fraud or misrepresentation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain transfer pricing documentation or use non-arm's length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty up to $100,000 per transaction; interest on tax adjustments; possible reassessment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability if knowingly participating in non-compliant arrangements

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring transactions to evade anti-money laundering reporting or sanctions screening
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to $500,000; criminal charges under Proceeds of Crime Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, imprisonment, and disqualification from directorships
